From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@greenridgebank.com>

Cc: security@greenridgebank.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: IRP & postmortem for 2026-08-19 event

Hi Grace,

Thank you for the quick responses earlier. As part of our internal audit and board briefing, we need a formal incident closure package for the event on 2026-08-19. Specifically we are requesting: 

- The incident response plan (IRP) you used for containment and remediation;
- A short postmortem describing root cause, impact, and timeline;
- Telemetry samples / sanitized logs showing the detection and containment window;
- A recommended redaction map for anything that might contain customer PII.

We need this delivered to our security mailbox (security@greenridgebank.com) and shared to our secure Drive link by EOD Monday 2026-08-23. If there are items that cannot be shared (for legal or third-party reasons), please flag them and provide a summary.

Can you confirm you can deliver this and whether you expect any follow-up questions from our legal/compliance teams?

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Information Security
GreenRidge Bank
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@greenridgebank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: IRP & postmortem for 2026-08-19 event

Lena — thanks for the clear list and the deadline. We can deliver a redacted closure packet by EOD Monday (2026-08-23). High-level plan: 

1) Internal compendium: redacted IRP + short postmortem (2-3 pages)
2) Forensics: CSV timeline + representative telemetry samples (sanitized)
3) Redaction map (spreadsheet) showing fields removed or pseudonymized
4) Legal/third-party notes where full artifacts cannot be shared

Action items on our side: I will compile the packet and loop in Marissa for the forensic timeline and telemetry extracts. Jonas, can you confirm legal review cadence so we don’t miss any export restrictions?

Lena — quick questions so we scope correctly: 
- Do you want the full network packet-headers/pcap extracts or just application telemetry + auth logs?
- Any specific fields you want preserved for board review (e.g., anonymized customer IDs)?

I’ll put the deliverables into a shared Drive folder and send the secure link when ready.

—Grace O'Connor
Sr. Manager, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@greenridgebank.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Forensics timeline and artifact list for GR-20260819

Forwarding the preliminary timeline and artifact inventory. Attachments included: forensics_timeline-20260819.csv, telemetry_sample-20260819.json, redaction_map.xlsx. Notes: 

- The timeline is event-driven (detection -> containment -> remediation) with UTC timestamps. Columns: step, start_utc, end_utc, actor, notes.
- Telemetry sample is sanitized; customer identifiers replaced with stable pseudonyms (GR_CUST_###). Full logs were scoped out per our third-party license and legal guidance.
- Redaction map flags fields we recommend removing from any shared packet. Sensitive fields: full IPs (recommend /24 anonymize), raw session tokens, and internal hostnames.

Lena — I highlighted two items that require a brief legal note: (1) a third-party telemetry collector (vendor X) retains raw traces under their contract; (2) aggregated metrics we can share, but not raw DB query samples. If either of those is a blocker for your board package, let me know and we can generate an alternate summary.

Subject: GreenRidge - Incident closure packet and redaction request

Lena / Grace / Marissa — final packet delivered. See attached: GR_IRP_v2_redacted.pdf (redacted incident response plan), forensics_timeline-20260819.csv, telemetry_sample-20260819.json, redaction_map.xlsx. Also uploaded to the secure Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/greenridge/closure-packet

Summary (2 bullets for your board):
- Root cause: misconfigured health-check endpoint exposed a tokenized admin path; attacker exploited a delegated key with limited scope. Containment occurred within 27 minutes of detection; no evidence of data exfiltration beyond metadata-level traces per our telemetry.
- Remediation: revoked delegated keys, rotated affected credentials, applied a validation rule to the health-check path, and added canonical monitoring rules. Post-deployment validation run completed on 2026-08-21.

Redaction notes: we removed raw IPs and customer-identifying records. The redaction_map.xlsx documents each removed field and rationale. Where raw artifacts are held by a vendor, we included a signed attestation and a short summary.

If your legal/compliance team wants the vendor-held raw traces under an NDA addendum, we can initiate that handoff (estimated 3–5 business days).

Please confirm receipt and let us know if you want a 30-minute walkthrough with the forensics and operations team. I am available Wed/Thu afternoons PST.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
